chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim the Commentator (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar narrated to us on the authority of their fathers, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Rida, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said: A man stood up to al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, describe your Lord for us, for those before us have differed with us.' Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:

Verily, he who describes his Lord by analogy remains in ambiguity throughout time, straying from the straight path, wandering in deviation, led astray from the way, and saying what is not proper. I know Him by what He made known about Himself without vision, and I describe Him by what He described Himself without form. He is not perceived by the senses, nor comparable to humans. He is known without resemblance, and is distant with no equal. He is not represented by His creation, nor does He act unjustly in His judgment. The creation are submissive to what He knows, and proceed upon what He has inscribed in the hidden Book. They do not act contrary to what He knows of them, nor do they desire anyone else. He is Near but not attached, and Far but not cut off. He is Ascertained but not exemplified, and One but not divided. He is known by the Signs, and established by the Symbols. Hence, there is no god but He, the Great, the Most High.

key_terms.الْقِيَاس: Analogy or comparison used to describe God

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida describe the attributes and nature of God in response to questions about divine description?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid* by distinguishing between God's self-known essence and human conceptualization, warning that analogical reasoning (*qiyas*) leads to theological confusion. This narration reinforces the principle of *Tanzih* (transcendence), asserting that while God is near to creation, He remains distinct and incomparable, known through His signs rather than sensory perception or physical representation.
